Guerneville, California · bring the bike

Should you bring your bike to Guerneville?

Bring it if you are staying more than a day or two, and plan on a car.

The short answer, in full

We found no bike shop in Guerneville. The nearest is a repair and rental shop in Forestville, about 6 miles east in a straight line. The widest rental fleet is in Santa Rosa, about 16 miles off. The airport is close: Sonoma County (STS), about 10 miles east in a straight line. American, Delta and Southwest all check a packed bike at the standard bag fee (Nov 2026). No shop near the river says it takes a shipped bike.

Fly itShip itRent oneGet aroundThe rules

Flying to Guerneville with a bike

  1. Charles M. Schulz–Sonoma County Airport (STS)

    • 10 mi from Guerneville

    The close one, about 10 miles east in a straight line.

    More about STS

    The drive is longer. Four airlines fly here, by the airport’s passenger FAQ (modified Oct 9, 2026). Alaska: Boise, Burbank, Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Orange County, Palm Springs, Phoenix, Portland, San Diego, Seattle. American: Phoenix, Dallas-Fort Worth. Southwest: Denver, Burbank, San Diego, Las Vegas. Delta: Salt Lake City. Nine rental car brands on site, counters in baggage claim: ACE, Avis, Budget, Enterprise, Hertz, National, NextCar, Dollar, Thrifty (the airport’s car-rental page). The curb in front of the terminal is the pick-up zone. The airport’s pages say nothing about bikes, oversized bags or any service to Guerneville. 2200 Airport Boulevard, Santa Rosa; (707) 565-7243.

  2. San Francisco International (SFO)

    • 70 mi from Guerneville

    About 70 miles southeast in a straight line.

    More about SFO

    Groome Transportation runs 17 buses a day each way between SFO and Sonoma County, about 2.25 to 2.5 hours to the STS stop, from $39 one way (Nov 2026). Its FAQ says it takes bicycles at no extra charge and asks riders to limit their luggage. It doesn’t say whether that means a boxed bike, so call ahead with a case. That gets a bike to Santa Rosa, not to the river.

  3. Oakland International (OAK)

    • 69 mi from Guerneville

    About 69 miles southeast in a straight line.

    More about OAK

    Groome runs 7 buses a day each way between OAK and Sonoma and Marin counties, about 2.25 hours to the STS stop, $55 one way (Nov 2026), on minibuses. Same bike line in its FAQ.

What the airlines charge

From each airline’s own page, Nov 2026, unless marked.

Airline by airline

American: one non-motorized touring, mountain, tandem or racing bike in a hard case, a bike bag or a box built for bikes; standard checked bag fee up to 50 lb, standard overweight fee from 50 to 70 lb, oversize fees do not apply; not in a hard case it is treated as fragile. Main Cabin first bag $45 online or $50 at the airport, second $55 or $60, for tickets issued on or after April 9, 2026; Basic Economy $50 or $55, second $60 or $65, for tickets from May 18, 2026; overweight $30 for 50 to 53 lb and $100 for 53 to 70 lb. Southwest: a non-motorized single-seat bike is checked baggage at standard bag and overweight fees, oversize waived; over 100 lb or 115 inches is refused; pedals and handlebars off and wrapped; cardboard or a soft case flies on a limited release. First bag $45, second $55 on Basic, Choice and Choice Preferred fares; 51 to 70 lb adds $100. Delta: a non-motorized touring or single-seat racing bike in a container built for bikes goes at the standard bag allowance and fee; over 50 lb pays an excess weight fee the page does not price; 100 lb or more, or over 115 linear inches, is refused; a hard-shell bike case needs no release, a soft bag signs one; some Delta Connection flights exclude bikes. First bag $45, second $55, US domestic Main. Alaska flies the most routes into STS. Alaska (Sept 2026): a cased bike is a standard checked bag, oversize waived and overweight waived to 70 lb, first bag $45, second $55; read its sports-equipment page before you book. Keep the case under 50 lb and it is one ordinary checked bag on American, Southwest and Delta.

Shipping your bike to Guerneville

No shop within reach of Guerneville says on its own site that it receives a shipped bike (Nov 16, 2026).

How shipping works here

Three will build one you bring in a box, or pack yours to go home, for a published fee. Revel Cycles in Sebastopol builds a bike from the box for $200 and packs one for $125; Sports Basement builds one from its box for $155 and boxes one for $110; Trek Bicycle Santa Rosa boxes one for $79.99 (Nov 2026). Russian River Cycle Service in Forestville is the nearest shop; its site says repair and rentals and nothing about shipping, boxing or assembly. Call (707) 887-2453 before you send anything, and note it is open Wednesday to Saturday only. BikeFlights ships by UPS and its help page gives no transit-day count. If a shop agrees to take it, ship at least a week ahead. Flying into STS with the bike is the simpler way.

Renting a bike near Guerneville

We found nothing to rent in Guerneville itself.

What renting costs and what you get

The county tourism office’s bike-rental list has no Guerneville or Monte Rio entry. The nearest road bikes are in Forestville; the widest choice is in Santa Rosa. The math: a cased bike is $45 each way on American, Southwest or Delta, so about $90 round trip (Nov 2026). Sports Basement’s alloy road bike is $75 for a day, $135 for two to four days and $220 for a week, so renting wins for a one-day ride and for anyone driving up without a bike, and it is close to even for a long weekend. For a week, for a fit you depend on, or for gravel, bring yours: the Santa Rosa store’s page doesn’t name gravel bikes. Sports Basement also rents a hard bike travel case ($55 a day, $80 for two to four days, $110 a week), which helps a rider flying home.

  1. Russian River Cycle Service

    Forestville, about 6 miles east in a straight line.

    Website
    More about Russian River Cycle Service

    Road bike $75 a day with a helmet and repair kit; hybrid $45 a day with helmet, basket, lock and pump (Nov 2026). The page gives no brand, frame, groupset or sizes: tell them your pedals and ask what the bike is. Rental appointments seven days a week; delivery offered.

  2. Sports Basement Santa Rosa

    Santa Rosa, about 16 miles southeast in a straight line.

    Website
    More about Sports Basement Santa Rosa

    Chain rates (Nov 2026): carbon road $100 a day, $175 for 2 to 4 nights, $300 for 5 to 9; aluminum road $75 a day; full-suspension carbon mountain bike $135 a day; e-bike $75 a day. Deposit required. Reserve online ahead; same-day in store with a smaller choice.

  3. Revel Cycles

    Sebastopol, about 12 miles southeast in a straight line.

    Website
    More about Revel Cycles

    E-bikes $75 for 3 hours or $95 a day; cruisers $50 a day (Nov 2026). Free cancellation up to 24 hours ahead. No road, gravel or mountain bikes.

Getting around Guerneville with a bike

You’ll want a car.

Yes, for most visitors.

Getting around, in full

We found no train and no airport shuttle to Guerneville. The nearest bike shop is about 6 miles east in a straight line, and the widest rental fleet is about 16 miles away in Santa Rosa. With a bike case, rent a car at STS (nine brands in the terminal) or book a large rideshare; a bus rack takes a built bike, not a box. With a built bike and no car it can be done. Sonoma County Transit’s Route 20 runs between Santa Rosa and Monte Rio through Sebastopol, Forestville, Rio Nido and Guerneville. Every bus has racks, and it stops on 3rd Street near the Railroad Square SMART station. It is a thin schedule. It’s one daily timetable with some weekday-only trips. Toward the river, the last bus that runs every day leaves Coddingtown at 5:20 pm (Route 20 timetable, effective April 12, 2026). Once you are in town with a built bike, downtown and the river are rideable; the roads out are the question, and that is in the rules and safety line. Caltrans has one-way signal control on Highway 116 west of town, between Sheridan Ranch Road and Vacation Beach, expected to last into early 2027 (advisory of July 30, 2026).

  • Transit: Sonoma County Transit (its bike page, Nov 2026): every bus has a front rack for two or three bikes, first come, first served, no extra fare.
Transit and bike share, in full

Transit: Sonoma County Transit (its bike page, Nov 2026): every bus has a front rack for two or three bikes, first come, first served, no extra fare. A bike can be up to 80 inches long, 48 tall and 24 wide. Standard two-wheeled bikes and e-bikes with sealed dry cell batteries only; no recumbents, tandems, three-wheelers or muddy bikes; fat tires must be deflated to fit; no front-mounted flat racks or folding baskets. You load it yourself. A folding bike can come inside if it stays out of the aisle. On the last trip of the day with a full rack, the driver may let a bike inside. The agency takes no responsibility for damage. Route 20 stops in Guerneville at Safeway and the West County Services Center; weekdays about 12 buses toward Santa Rosa and 10 back, fewer on weekends, when the trips marked Monday to Friday don’t run (timetable effective April 12, 2026). The page lists no fare. SMART, the train (policy modified Feb 25, 2026): up to 12 bikes a car, one per rider, space permitting and at the conductor’s call; e-bikes need working pedals and a sealed battery and cannot be charged on board; no tandems, three-wheelers, trailers or share bikes; walk the bike on the platform. The policy states no bike fee and no rush-hour rule. The SMART station nearest the airport is a mile from it, at Airport Boulevard and Regional Parkway; the SMART Connect shuttle links the two every day, 8 am to 6 pm, $1.50 (the airport’s page, 2026). No train comes closer to Guerneville than Santa Rosa.

Bike share: We found no bike share in Guerneville (Nov 2026). Rent from a shop, or stay at one of the three places that keep house bikes for guests.

The rules on the road in California

California law (Nov 2026).

Every rule, in full

Drivers must give three feet when passing a bike (Vehicle Code 21760); where a second lane runs the same way, the driver moves into it to pass if that is practicable; where three feet is not possible, the driver slows to a reasonable speed and passes only when it does not endanger the rider. The fine is $35, or $220 if a collision injures the rider (statute, Nov 11, 2026). Helmets are required under 18 (21212). E-bikes come in three classes (312.5): class 1 pedal-assist to 20 mph, class 2 throttle to 20 mph, class 3 pedal-assist to 28 mph with a speedometer, rider 16 or older and helmeted. Ride as far right as practicable except when passing, turning left, or in a lane too narrow to share (21202). No earbuds in both ears (27400). At night, a white headlight and a red rear reflector or light (21201). Sidewalk riding is set by each city and county (21206); we couldn’t find Sonoma County’s rule for unincorporated Guerneville, so walk the bike on Main Street’s sidewalks. CalBike’s page (modified Aug 24, 2026) lists no stop-as-yield law. The read, from the agencies: Sonoma County Regional Parks, making its case for a separated Lower Russian River Trail, calls the river corridor a “high-traffic, high-speed road with a history of multiple bicycle and pedestrian accidents” with “insufficient sidewalks, bike lanes and no shared use pathways”; that trail is still a proposal with no build date. Caltrans’ own Sept 1, 2026 document for Highway 116 from Monte Rio to near Sebastopol lists bike facilities as a top-tier need for the whole corridor. West of town, 116 is down to one lane under temporary signals between Sheridan Ranch Road and Vacation Beach into early 2027 (Caltrans, July 30, 2026); check before a spring trip.
